info.title: Totalis Hyperliquid API
info.description:
REST API for Totalis singles and parlays on Hyperliquid HIP-4 outcome markets, for client integrations and external market makers.

There are three ways in, each sent as `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`:

- **Scoped API key** (`ttk_`), for servers, bots and market makers. The account owner creates it in the Totalis app, or a wallet-session user creates one with `POST /v1/me/api-keys` and a fresh wallet signature (see API keys). It acts for one account, yours or a maker's, with only the scopes it holds, and needs no `Origin`.
- **Wallet session**, for users who bring their own wallet to a partner's web page. The page signs the wallet in with `POST /v1/auth/wallet-challenges` and `POST /v1/auth/wallet-sessions`; the session is bound to the page's registered `Origin` and must be sent from it. Pages may also label their traffic with their publishable browser key in `X-Totalis-Partner: tpb_...`.
- **Partner server key** (`tpk_`), only for `POST /v1/partner/wallet-admissions`, which lets a new wallet open its account during the invite-only launch. Server to server, never in a browser, and never with an `Origin`.

Public market reads need no credential. A credential only authenticates: every bet, cash-out and withdrawal also carries the wallet or maker signature the HyperEVM contract verifies. An external wallet sends `POST /v1/core-exits` to move its vault cash to HyperCore before a HyperCore order.

For access, partner credentials (origins, browser and server keys), builder codes or staging, email [founders@totalis.trade](mailto:founders@totalis.trade).

Amounts are base-10 strings in native USDC atomic units, large identifiers are decimal strings, and every command `POST` requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Every error is `{error: {code, message, retry, request_id, field_violations}}`. `code` is stable; each operation lists the codes it returns per status. `retry` is `NEVER` (stop), `BACKOFF` (resend the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key` after `Retry-After` seconds) or `REFRESH` (re-read state, then send a new request with a new key). `field_violations` names invalid inputs by JSON pointer, such as `/legs/0/side`.

owner.description: Current position owner, who sells the ticket back.

expiry.description: Unix seconds after which the quote can no longer be executed.

salt.description: Random uint256, as a decimal string, that makes each signed quote unique.

leg_state.description: Position leg state the quote was priced against; must equal the RFQ's leg_state.

SellBackTerms.description: Sell-back terms: the underwriting maker buys the position back and it closes. They mirror the signed SellBack struct.

SeriesId.description: Series key: the first 16 lowercase hex characters of the SHA-256 of v1|network|template|subject|expiry, where network is mainnet or testnet; for a price series template is binaryPrice or priceTouch, subject the perp name and expiry its decimal Unix seconds; for an IPO ladder template is companyIpoFirstDayMarketCap, subject the trimmed company and expiry the listing deadline's decimal Unix seconds. Thresholds and membership are not part of the key.

SeriesMarket.description: A series or game member: a standalone market with no Hyperliquid question.

side.description: Market side the label belongs to, YES or NO.

label.description: Display label for the side; null when a templated name cannot be rendered from a qualified template.

chain_id.description: HyperEVM chain ID for the transaction: 998 testnet or 999 mainnet.

data.description: Canonical ABI-encoded calldata built by the server; lowercase hex.

value.description: Native value in wei; always zero.

kind.description: Always `TRANSFER`: you take over the position.

deadline.description: Confirm before this instant, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp. A later answer cannot reopen the acceptance.

transfer.description: Accepted transfer terms; sign them as `CashoutTransfer`.

TransferMakerAcceptance.description: An owner's accept of your transfer quote.
TransferMakerAcceptance.title: Transfer acceptance

quote_id.description: Quote ID: the EIP-712 digest of `transfer` as the `CashoutTransfer` struct, which the owner signs to accept.

kind.description: Always `TRANSFER`: another maker takes over the position.

sequence.description: Venue-wide publication sequence number; a higher value was created later.

transfer.description: Transfer terms the owner accepts by signing `quote_id` as `CashoutTransfer`.

TransferQuote.description: A cash-out offer from another maker: it pays the owner `price` and takes over the position.
TransferQuote.title: Transfer quote

position_id.description: Position the quote is for; the signed CashoutTransfer names it ticketId.

price.description: Price the buyer pays the seller for the whole position, in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

seller.description: Current position owner, who sells the ticket.

buyer.description: The bidding maker's current quote signer, which becomes the owner and pays from its own vault balance.

expiry.description: Unix seconds after which the quote can no longer be executed.

salt.description: Random uint256, as a decimal string, that makes each signed quote unique.

leg_state.description: Position leg state the quote was priced against; must equal the RFQ's leg_state.

TransferTerms.description: Transfer terms: another maker buys the position and becomes its owner. They mirror the signed CashoutTransfer struct.

label.description: Your name for the key, 1 to 80 characters.

scopes.description: Permissions the key holds; each must apply to the account, as the capabilities route lists.

expires_in_days.description: Lifetime in days, 1 to 90, or 0 for no expiry; 30 when omitted.

UnsignedCreateKeyRequest.description: The exact key request the account owner signs. Scopes must apply to the account.

UnsignedMetric.description: Non-negative amount in atomic USDC (6 decimals, "1000000" = 1 USDC); null when it could not be established, never zero in its place.

overlap_seconds.description: How long the old key keeps working after the rotation, 0 to 86400 seconds; 3600 when omitted.

expires_in_days.description: The replacement's lifetime in days, 1 to 90, or 0 for no expiry; 30 when omitted.

UnsignedRotateKeyRequest.description: The exact rotation request the account owner signs; the replacement inherits the old key's account, label and scopes.

Username.description: 3 to 20 lowercase letters, digits or underscores. Unique across accounts.

VaultWithdrawal.description: Owner-signed EIP-712 Exit that moves the withdrawal's shortfall from the vault to the embedded wallet; Totalis relays it and pays gas. The signed Exit's account and to are both the caller's embedded wallet, which the venue fills in.

amount.description: Shortfall in atomic USDC (6 decimals): the withdrawal amount minus spendable wallet USDC; must be greater than zero.

expiry.description: Exit expiry in Unix seconds; must be at least 5 seconds ahead and at most 3600 seconds ahead, less a 5-second clock-skew margin.

salt.description: Caller-chosen uint256 as a decimal string that makes the signed Exit unique.

signature.description: Signature by the embedded wallet over the EIP-712 Exit(account,to,amount,expiry,salt) digest, with account and to the wallet; ECDSA or ERC-1271 contract signature bytes.

status.description: Account status: ACTIVE, RESTRICTED (some actions are refused by policy) or CLOSED.

username.description: The account's public username and the name of its /r/ link, or null until it picks one with PUT /v1/me/username or takes a generated one with POST /v1/me/username. It can change. Servers before contract 129 omit it.

avatar_seed.description: Random seed assigned when the account is created; the account can change it with PUT /v1/me/avatar. Clients draw the account's generated avatar from it, so the avatar is the same on every device. Servers before contract 134 omit it.

wallet.description: The account's wallet: its Privy embedded wallet, or the one wallet of an account that signs in with an external wallet. It is the account's owner, which signs API-key issuance, and its signer, which signs its financial actions.

wallet_kind.description: EMBEDDED for a Privy embedded wallet, whose free vault cash Totalis moves to HyperCore in the background; EXTERNAL for an account that signs in with an external wallet, which has no such sweep. Servers before contract 147 omit it.

admitted_at.description: When the partner first admitted the wallet; the same on every retry.

address.description: The wallet that may create its account at its next sign-in.

consent.description: The wallet's consent to this partner: its personal_sign of the exact message whose lines are `Allow <slug> to open a Totalis account for this wallet.`, `This does not authorize a financial action.`, an empty line, `Wallet: <lowercase address>`, `Partner: <slug>`, `Environment: <development|staging|production>`, `Chain ID: <chain>` and `Expires At: <expires_at>`, joined by newlines. The SDK builds it (admissionConsentMessage).

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC, after now and at most 24 hours ahead, signed exactly as sent.

signature.description: The wallet's personal_sign signature over the consent message.

challenge_id.description: Send it with the signature to POST /v1/auth/wallet-sessions.

message.description: The exact EIP-4361 message to sign with personal_sign.

issued_at.description: When the challenge was issued, RFC 3339 UTC.

expires_at.description: Five minutes after issued_at; exchange the signature before then.

WalletChallengeRequest.description: Asks for a SIWE message proving control of an externally owned wallet. The message names the origin, chain, nonce and the Idempotency-Key as its Request ID, and expires after 5 minutes.

address.description: The wallet signing in. An address holding contract code is refused with WALLET_CONTRACT_UNSUPPORTED.

origin.description: Must equal the request's Origin header exactly.

WalletFunding.description: A USDC EIP-3009 ReceiveWithAuthorization moving value from the caller's embedded wallet into the vault. The venue fills from and account with that wallet; sign the message with both set to it.

kind.description: Funding source: WALLET pays the shortfall from the caller's embedded wallet.

value.description: Atomic USDC (6 decimals) drawn from the wallet into the vault. It must equal the exact stake shortfall over free vault cash at admission.

valid_after.description: EIP-3009 validAfter in Unix seconds; must not be in the future.

valid_before.description: EIP-3009 validBefore in Unix seconds; must be at least 5 seconds ahead and at most 900 seconds after valid_after.

salt.description: Random 32 bytes; the EIP-3009 nonce is keccak256(abi.encode(vault, chainId, from, salt, account)), with from and account the embedded wallet.

authorization_signature.description: 65-byte ECDSA signature by the embedded wallet over the USDC ReceiveWithAuthorization message, with the vault as payee.

WalletSession.description: A bearer session for the wallet's account. It lasts at most 30 days and ends after 7 days without an API request, or at logout. It authenticates the account; every bet, cash-out and withdrawal still needs the wallet's own signature.

token_type.description: Always Bearer: send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

access_token.description: The session token. It works only with the Origin it signed in from; keep it out of URLs and logs.

address.description: The signed-in wallet, which is the account's wallet.

issued_at.description: When the session was issued, RFC 3339 UTC.

expires_at.description: The 30-day cap; the 7-day idle limit can end the session sooner.

WalletSessionRequest.description: Proves the challenge with the wallet's personal_sign signature over the exact message.

challenge_id.description: The challenge_id from POST /v1/auth/wallet-challenges; each proves one session.

signature.description: The wallet's personal_sign signature over the challenge's exact message.

destination.description: External address that receives the USDC.

amount.description: Total amount sent to destination, in atomic USDC (6 decimals).

shortfall_amount.description: Part of amount first withdrawn from the vault to the wallet, in atomic USDC; "0" when the wallet already covered it.

status.description: VAULT_WITHDRAWAL_QUEUED: the vault top-up is queued and the payout waits for it; PAYOUT_SUBMITTED: the payout is queued or relayed; PAYOUT_COMMITTED: destination received amount (terminal); FAILED: the withdrawal stopped and nothing left the Totalis balance: a vault top-up that committed stays in the wallet (terminal).

vault_operation_id.description: Operation of the vault top-up; null when there is no shortfall.

payout_operation_id.description: Operation of the relayed payout; null until the vault top-up commits.

payout_transaction_hash.description: HyperEVM transaction of the payout; null until it is broadcast.

updated_at.description: When the withdrawal last changed, RFC3339 UTC.

WithdrawalCommand.description: The whole withdrawal in one request: pay amount from the embedded wallet to destination, topping the wallet up from the vault first when it cannot cover the amount. The owner signs the vault Exit for the shortfall and the USDC payout together; Totalis relays both, in order, and pays the gas.

destination.description: External address that receives the USDC.

amount.description: Total amount to send, in atomic USDC (6 decimals); must be greater than zero.

vault_withdrawal.description: Signed Exit moving the exact shortfall (amount minus spendable wallet USDC) from the vault back to the embedded wallet. Required when there is a shortfall and forbidden when there is none; a mismatch returns 409 STATE_CONFLICT with retry REFRESH: re-read balances and sign again.

payout_authorization.description: The embedded wallet's USDC EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization of exactly amount to destination. Its nonce is not sent: sign keccak256(abi.encode(keccak256("TOTALIS_PAYOUT_NONCE_V1"), chainId, vault, account, uint128(Idempotency-Key))), where account is the embedded wallet and Idempotency-Key is this request's key read as 16 bytes. The signature is therefore bound to this request and cannot start a second withdrawal. Choose the `Idempotency-Key` before you sign.

valid_after.description: EIP-3009 validAfter in Unix seconds; must not be in the future.

valid_before.description: EIP-3009 validBefore in Unix seconds: at least 300 seconds after vault_withdrawal.expiry (or after now when there is no shortfall), so the payout can still be relayed once the vault leg lands, and at most 4500 seconds after valid_after.

authorization_signature.description: 65-byte ECDSA signature by the embedded wallet over the USDC TransferWithAuthorization(from=wallet, to=destination, value=amount, validAfter, validBefore, nonce) message.

ApiKeysRetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before resending the same request.

CacheControl.description: Always `no-store`; account data must not be cached.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before resending the same request

Vary.description: The response varies by the Authorization header, so shared caches must not reuse it across credentials.

apiKey.description: Scoped API key (`ttk_...`), created in the Totalis app or by a wallet-session user through the API keys routes with a fresh wallet signature; those routes never accept a key. Each key acts for one account, yours or a maker's, and holds only scopes that account can use. Each operation lists the scopes it requires. Send no `Origin`.

walletSession.description: Wallet session: the `access_token` from `POST /v1/auth/wallet-sessions`, for a user who brings their own wallet to a partner's web page. It acts for that wallet's account with no scope limit, and is bound to the `Origin` it signed in from: send exactly one `Origin` header with that value, or the request is `ORIGIN_REQUIRED` or `UNAUTHENTICATED`. It lasts at most 30 days and ends after 7 idle days or at `DELETE /v1/auth/wallet-sessions/current`.

partnerServerKey.description: Partner server key (`tpk_...`), issued by Totalis to a registered partner. It calls only `POST /v1/partner/wallet-admissions`, from the partner's server with no `Origin`; it cannot act for an account. Never ship it to a browser: pages use the publishable browser key (`X-Totalis-Partner: tpb_...`), which labels traffic but authorizes nothing.
